description: Somos un equipo interesados por la tecnología y el planeta. Buscamos desarrollar una herramienta que nos ayude a difundir conocimiento respecto a nuestro hermoso planeta. ¡Estamos en busca de mentes curiosas y creativas que quieran aportar nuevas perspectivas!
summary:
We developedx a free, browser-based web application developed by Team "Planeta Huellitas" that transforms official NASA GISS climate data (GISTEMP v4, CMIP6 radiative forcing, and the Common Sense Climate Index) into an interactive audiovisual experience. Built with Python, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and the Web Audio API, the prototype acts as a virtual turntable featuring seven playable "discs" covering global and summer temperatures (1880–2025), 50-year warming acceleration, 2100 radiative forcing projections, greenhouse gases versus aerosols, solar/volcanic activity, and human climate perception.

To address "The Earth Information Jukebox" challenge, the application turns raw scientific tables into a 38-second multisensory playback. As the virtual tonearm moves across each disc, normalized climate values shift ring colors from blue to red while artistically controlling musical pitch, dissonance, and percussion density, paired with visual comparison sliders, interactive timelines, and screen-reader descriptions.

This project is important because it makes long-term climate trends immediately intuitive without requiring users to read spreadsheets. It provides an accessible, installation-free learning alternative for people with low vision or auditory learning styles, while demonstrating a reusable model for translating open NASA data into engaging public insights.
details:
"Time-Travel DJ" is a web application created by our team to turn official NASA GISS climate records into an interactive audiovisual experience. Rather than presenting Earth's history through static spreadsheets, we reimagined climate data as a retro vinyl jukebox featuring seven playable "discs" based on three open datasets: global and summer temperature anomalies from 1880 to 2025 (GISTEMP v4), historical and projected radiative forcing up to 2100 (CMIP6 GISS-E2.1-G), and the Common Sense Climate Index.

To bring this concept to life, we built a two-part system. First, a Python script using pandas, numpy, and matplotlib cleans, filters, and normalizes the raw scientific files into lightweight JSON configurations and dynamic charts. Second, a browser-based interface built with HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and the Web Audio API runs a 38-second virtual turntable. As the tonearm moves across a selected disc, its rings shift from cool blue to warm red, comparison sliders reveal past-versus-present maps or live graphs, and normalized climate values dynamically control musical pitch, dissonance, and percussion density.

By translating complex scientific series into real-time sound and color, our project makes long-term climate trends immediately intuitive and emotionally engaging. Throughout development—supported by Figma for layout design, GitHub for hosting, and AI tools (Claude and Gemini) for coding and documentation guidance—we prioritized scientific transparency, smooth browser performance, and accessibility. The final prototype is completely free, requires no installation, includes live text descriptions for screen readers, and offers an easily expandable model for helping diverse audiences hear and understand our changing planet.
